problem_text:
A city aims to devise a wastewater purification strategy to lower total nitrogen discharge from several industrial effluent outfalls. Currently, no treatment procedures have been implemented.

The discharge profile for each outfall is as follows:
* For Outfall A, the discharge coefficient is 2.782, and the flow rate is 209.737.
* For Outfall B, the discharge coefficient is 2.676, and the flow rate is 202.243.
* For Outfall C, the discharge coefficient is 1.246, and the flow rate is 88.21.

To abate the discharge, several purification technologies can be employed, each with a distinct removal efficacy:
* Technology X achieves a 29% reduction in contaminant load.
* Technology Y achieves a 47% reduction in contaminant load.
* Technology Z achieves a 28% reduction in contaminant load.

Deploying a technology at an outfall introduces an incremental cost per unit of flow. The cost matrix for all outfall–technology pairings is provided:

| Outfall \ Technology | Technology X | Technology Y | Technology Z |
|---|---|---|---|
| Outfall A | 110.767 | 10.109 | 71.59 |
| Outfall B | 13.701 | 186.529 | 176.957 |
| Outfall C | 168.016 | 68.428 | 21.006 |

The decision involves selecting which technologies to apply to each outfall (outfalls may implement multiple technologies concurrently), and an outfall may also retain a portion of its flow untreated if required.
The objective is to guarantee that the aggregate nitrogen discharge is diminished by at least a fraction P = 0.639 of the baseline load, while minimizing the aggregate expenditure.
